notes: Both coders found the same two TLC documents (delegates, three tiers) and matched on 67 units. Main disagreements: (1) policy_type for reflect-before-policy advice (A P63, B UNCOVERED) and the crowdsourced-syllabus-bank sentence (A P63, B P04), resolved to P63 with fit_notes; the embedded-AI sentence (P61 vs P07) and the purpose sentence (P04 vs P56) resolved by the passage stating a fact or scope rather than a rule; the UCLA free-tools sentence (P51 vs P92) resolved to P92. (2) Phase on the sample-statement rules and survey evidence (general vs during-work, general vs over-time), resolved by the codebook definitions and the 'class assignments' wording. (3) Modality of the 'treated as academic dishonesty' consequence (informs vs must), resolved to must; the 'could include' option for the three sample statements, resolved to may. (4) Unit stance on benefit, literacy and discussion sentences (encourage vs neutral), resolved to neutral unless the sentence recommends use. A-only units (6: environmental e-waste and water, benefits of chatbots, faculty chart, sample survey, accessibility warning) and B-only units (2 P25 pointers to APA/MLA citation guidance, 1 reflect-on-courses sentence) were all real statements in the source and were kept. Stance agreed in both documents.
